title: Rewrite
text: Write $$\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}$$ as $$x^{\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)}$$. An antiderivative is $$\frac{3}{2} x^{\frac{2}{3}}$$.

title: Take the limit
text: At $$x=1$$ the antiderivative is $$\frac{3}{2}$$, and as $$x$$ approaches $$0$$ from the right it goes to $$0$$. So the integral is $$\frac{3}{2}$$.
